A bounded claim-query working set

Separate native PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence compared one claim-query sample on equal-cardinality fresh databases. An indexed candidate prefix and point partition lock replaced a full active-backlog aggregate/sort. These are query observations, not full-application speedup measurements.

'+''.join(query_rows)+'
One recorded sample per scenario; timings include measurement noise
Pending eventsDormant partitionsBefore msAfter msShared buffer hits

The window considers up to 128 enabled candidate events. If every candidate partition is locked, a worker backs off until the prefix makes progress. This is an explicit fairness tradeoff. Paused-source/dead-index entries and vacuum health can still increase physical reads.

' 147 document='''OrderFlow · measured workload analysis

ENGINEERING EVIDENCE · 23 NOVEMBER 2026

OrderFlow: throughput, queuing and correctness

Repeated synthetic HTTP-to-worker trials, with exact reconciliation of accepted identities, immutable revisions, current records, history, receipts, checkpoints and tenant isolation. Every plotted trial completed and removed its owned database. These measurements cover the ingestion and materialization core.

'''+panels+'''

Read the measurements correctly

  • Each trial accepts 94% distinct valid revisions, 5% distinct-identity duplicate revisions, and 1% business-invalid currency events. A further 10% HTTP identity replay gives 110,000 attempts for the larger workload. Quarantine is an expected, independently checked outcome.
  • HTTP acceptance and terminal visibility answer different questions. The visibility measure is an upper-bound measure using the first independent observation of committed terminal state minus ingestion time on the database clock. It includes polling and query overhead. A stored transaction marker is not labeled an exact commit timestamp.
  • All three repetitions are retained for both configurations. Throughput is distinct terminal receipts divided by elapsed HTTP start-to-observed-drain time. The lines show throughput medians. Individual latency p95 values remain separate; they are not averaged into a pooled percentile.
  • Each trial ran in a separate private 2-vCPU, 4-GiB microVM from the same immutable prepared snapshot, using PostgreSQL 18.6 and Python 3.12.14. Host, cache and filesystem noise remain. The comparison does not isolate a causal worker-count speedup.
  • This is a bounded closed-loop synthetic HTTP load with up to 24 in-flight HTTP requests from 24 consumer tasks and real PostgreSQL/workers. It is not an open-loop arrival-rate capacity test, a hosted service SLO, dbt/Airflow throughput, or customer impact.
  • A practical next measurement is a controlled arrival-rate sweep on the same reserved host, recording queue age and CPU/I/O saturation. These observations do not establish unlimited scaling or a general latency guarantee.

Core + migrations SHA-256: '''+html.escape(large['source']['sha256'])+'''

Small gate SHA-256: '''+digest(SMALL)+'''
Large series SHA-256: '''+digest(LARGE)+'''

Prepared snapshot: snap_VroLt6lB8PEDt5AnT6r1LtpdJEf0. Raw inputs, truth ledgers, HTTP attempts and terminal observations are bound in the release manifest.

OrderFlow case study
